transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-04-01
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Glyph ML Eng), Tom Alvarez (Glyph Platform), Samantha Li (Glyph DS)

Summary (auto): weekly POC check-in for caching work. Reviewed latest KV/prefix hit rates and tuning knobs; agreed on stress test and data share.

00:00 Maya Chen: okay everyone uh thanks for joining, we'll do a quick agenda - run through last weeks results, tuning notes, open questions, and next steps. Diego is going to walk the numbers first.
00:18 Diego Ramos: cool, thanks Maya. So from the lab runs over the last 48 hours we saw prefix hit rate move from around 62% to roughly 78% for the canonical prompt groups after we normalized template tokens and enforced a 256 token prefix limit. note, these are measured on the check-in cluster not the dedicate pool so YMMV.
00:38 Priya Singh: quick q, when you say "canonical prompt groups" are you deduping slot values or normalizing user IDs? like what was the exact pre-processing?
00:50 Diego Ramos: yeah good call. we do lightweight canonicalization: strip unique ids, map dates to YYYY-mm-dd, lowercase free text for the cache key, and we hash parameter blobs. we found a lot of cache misses were because tiny differences in spacing and punctuation created different keys.
01:08 Tom Alvarez: sounds promising. did you also include model version in the cache key? we have strict rollout policies so we want to avoid cross-version pollution.
01:18 Diego Ramos: yes model version and route tag are part of the key. temperature and sampling flags are included for safety. we also added a TTL per key of 6 hours for this run to avoid stale prefix reuse for dynamic prompts.
01:32 Samantha Li: what about very short prompts, does caching even help there? we saw some regression in recall for a couple of generative flows when we cached too aggressively.
01:45 Diego Ramos: good point. we implemented a minimum prefix token threshold of 8 tokens to be eligible for caching. tiny prompts skip the cache to avoid returning stale completions. also we excluded prompts flagged as session-sensitive.
01:58 Maya Chen: can you share the impact on latency? that's what the product team cares about.
02:04 Diego Ramos: p50 improved modestly, p99 improved more - baseline p99 on the check cluster was ~620ms, after tuning p99 is ~420ms for cached prefix hits. For cache miss paths latencies roughly same as baseline. overall token throughput increased by circa 18% under continuous batching. (note: these numbers are noisy, see Diego's logs).
02:28 Priya Singh: those p99 numbers look good, curious about hit distribution over time. is the 78% sustained or just warm-cache snapshot?
02:38 Diego Ramos: current is warm-cache snapshot during steady-state with realistic replay traffic; we also did a 30-minute cold-restart test which dropped to ~45% until the cache warmed. that's why we want the 24h stress run.
02:52 Tom Alvarez: memory footprint — any evictions? we run a tight GPU mem profile on our Dedicated sim.
03:00 Diego Ramos: yes evictions occurred during spikes. we surfaced an eviction log and a histogram, evictions mostly for very long prefixes and low-frequency keys. recommendation: LRU with a hard cap plus segmented cache for hot prefixes. also consider prefix trimming for >512 token prefixes.
03:18 Priya Singh: what about prefix reuse strategy? our workload has many templated queries where only user name changes — we want to maximize reuse without leaking PII.
03:30 Diego Ramos: for PII we recommend canonicalization + token redaction before forming cache key and optionally replace PII with placeholders. also reuse at template level: keep a canonicalized prompt template registry and run a quick fingerprint to map an incoming prompt to template id plus slot hash. this increases prefix reuse dramatically.
03:55 Samantha Li: hm ok, any automated tooling to suggest templates?
04:00 Diego Ramos: we have a heuristic script that clusters prompts by edit distance and token overlap, outputs candidate templates and suggested canonicalization rules. we'll share a gist.
04:14 Maya Chen: action item there for Priya to upload the sample prompt set.
04:20 Priya Singh: will do, I'll try to include the top-50 prefixes and a handful of session flows.
04:26 Maya Chen: also we discussed fallback model behavior last week — how does fallback interact with cache keys?
04:32 Diego Ramos: fallback is model-aware: we version the cache and route on model alias, fallback path doesn't read keys for the primary model; we copy over compatible entries only if model family is compatible and tokenization identical. otherwise we avoid cross-model hits to reduce quality drift.
04:50 Tom Alvarez: anything on cost impact? our finance folks want numbers for projected savings.
04:55 Diego Ramos: roughly estimating, for this workload the improved hit rate would reduce token generation by ~20% on the host side which maps to roughly a 12-18% cost delta depending on batching and reserved pricing. Maya can put a more formal estimate in the pricing doc.
05:12 Maya Chen: yep I'll include a breakdown in the reserved capacity estimate. Diego can you run the 24h stress so we have stable numbers?
05:18 Diego Ramos: yep I'll run it on the dedicated-ish cluster tomorrow and share logs and a CSV with hourly hit rates.
05:25 Priya Singh: any security/compliance concerns? we need to ensure KMS keys for logs and an audit trail for cache evictions for SOC2.
05:34 Maya Chen: Redwood keeps audit logs for cache operations in the private deployment and can integrate with your KMS for encryption at rest. we'll share the security checklist.
05:44 Tom Alvarez: can you share the eviction logs format and retention policy?
05:48 Diego Ramos: sure, eviction logs will include key-fingerprint, timestamp, action, reason, current cache_size; we'll keep rolling logs for 7 days by default and can extend as needed.
05:58 Samantha Li: small nit — we saw some mis-attribution in the transcript from last time where "KV cache" was transcribed as "K V cake" which was kind of funny.
06:07 Maya Chen: haha yeah those transcriptions are not perfect.
06:10 Diego Ramos: other tuning knobs we tried: batching window shrink from 50ms to 30ms for low-latency flows, and continuous KV prefetch for hot templates. Prefetch increased hit rate during cold starts by about 8%.
06:26 Priya Singh: great, so final list of deliverables: prompt set from us, 24h stress test from you, pricing & reserved estimate from Maya, schedule dedicated benchmark.
06:36 Maya Chen: sounds right. any other questions?
06:40 Tom Alvarez: just confirm the benchmark date — can we target 2025-04-08?
06:44 Maya Chen: yes I'll send a calendar invite after the call.
06:47 Diego Ramos: I'll also attach the eviction histogram and a CSV of recent hit rates to the ticket.
06:52 Priya Singh: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
06:55 Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in the thread.
